decision.title: Source code as XML: tree-sitter trees with highlights captures (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , , , . The owner's order: the book first (Chapter "Source Code as XML"), then the grammars' own tests, then the implementation.

item.p: Shape (glossary , , , ): a document node; one element per named syntax node, named by its kind, in no namespace; anonymous nodes (tokens) and the bytes between nodes are text, so string() of the document is the source exactly, and the document element holds the whole text, leading and trailing whitespace included. A child's field name is a field attribute. A token with a highlight or a field name becomes an sxml:token element so it can carry them; a named kind that is no NCName (an alias) an sxml:node element with kind. ERROR nodes are ERROR elements (tree-sitter's spelling); a node the parser inserted has missing="true", and a missing token also kind. The option positions adds line, column, end-line, end-column (from 1, columns in characters, so they agree with XPath string positions); off by default, so documents compare without them. sxml is bound to urn:sxml on the document element. Like iXML (), syntax errors are part of the result, not an error: tree-sitter recovers, and a query can count //ERROR.

Highlights (glossary , ): the grammar's queries/highlights.scm (the files its tree-sitter.json names, in that order) runs through the runtime's query API (ts_query_). Text predicates are the host's job: eq?, match?, any-of?, their not- and any- forms; match? uses sxml's regex engine (F&O 4.0, 6.1, no flags; the queries' Rust regexes are in the common subset, and one that does not compile makes the predicate false); #is-not? local holds and #is? local does not (no locals query: no node is a local variable); directives (#set!) and unknown predicates are ignored. Captures named _… only serve predicates. When several patterns capture one node, the *last** pattern wins: the grammars' queries start with (identifier) @variable and refine it later, and their highlight tests expect the refinement (with the first pattern winning, the name in function i() {} would be variable, where the test says function). The winner is the highlight attribute; nested captures stay nested. Locals (locals.scm) and injections (injections.scm) are not run: a later packet can add them in the same place.

API: sxml:parse-code($source as xs:string?, $language as xs:string, $options as map(*)? := {}) as document-node()? with options highlights (default true) and positions (default false), and sxml:code-languages() as xs:string*, in the new well-known namespace urn:sxml (name.h: SXML_NAMESPACE_SXML = 16, additive after , as added EXSLT; sxml's own functions and errors go there). An unknown language is sxml:unknown-language. A direct function rather than fn:invisible-xml's function-returning shape: a grammar here is a compiled-in name, not run-time data, so there is nothing to compile once. Optional feature sxml_source_code_feature() ("source-code", processor.h, additive), whose library_functions hold the two rows (), in sxml_all_optional_features(), so every shipped build has it (). CLI (): no new command or flag; sxml xpath and sxml xquery bind the prefix sxml as they bind bin and file; a stylesheet declares it ().

Languages (glossary ): option (a), vendored grammars compiled in: JSON, JavaScript (with JSX), Python, C, CSS, HTML and Go, from the tree-sitter organization's repositories (MIT), in third_party/tree-sitter-grammars/LANGUAGE (LICENSE, the generated src/, the highlights queries, test/, and VERSION with the commit), by tools/vendor-tree-sitter-grammar.sh. They join grammars/CMakeLists.txt's one grammar list as sxml_source_grammar_LANGUAGE, with the entry point renamed sxml_source_language_LANGUAGE (sxml's own JSON grammar keeps tree_sitter_json) and Clang's -fno-sanitize=function (upstream scanners declare (), compatible in C17). The language table and queries are generated into src/source_code_languages.c by tools/generate-source-code-languages.py; adding a language is vendor plus generate. Option (b), a host API to register a TSLanguage and a query, is not built: it would make tree-sitter's ABI part of sxml's public contract; it stays a proposal. Not shipped, by cost (native -O2 code and data of parser and scanner): TypeScript 1,413,409 and TSX 1,447,676 bytes, Rust 1,125,096, Bash 1,335,694, Markdown 368,665 plus its inline grammar 361,385; shipped: JSON 7,605, JavaScript 413,323, Python 459,815, C 618,257, CSS 114,067, HTML 19,702, Go 222,353 (1,854,622 in all). sxml's own XPath, XQuery and XML grammars are not offered: they serve sxml's parsers (markers, external-subset entry points) and have no highlights queries.

Mechanism (src/source_code.c, src/source_code_internal.h, src/function_library_source_code.c): tree-sitter parses (; its progress callback charges the bytes read to the call's step limit and cancels the parse past it); the query cursor's progress callback does the same; captures are recorded in allocator memory, sorted by node, one per node; one loop walks a TSTreeCursor with an explicit stack of "made an element" flags () and writes tree builder events into an arena tree of the processor, text by byte offset, so nothing is lost or doubled. The exemption (tree-sitter allocates with malloc) extends from the parse to the query step; parser, tree, query and cursors are freed before the function returns.

Tests (): each shipped grammar's test/corpus (452 trees) and test/highlight (187 assertions) are vendored with it; tests/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-driver.xq runs them through sxml xquery (public API only): the document's S-expression against the corpus tree (normalized as tree-sitter normalizes; field names compared only when the expected tree has some), and each <-/^ assertion against the highlight attributes covering its line and column. tree-sitter/suite keeps a baseline that only goes up.

Done (commits e29713d book, 3b52502 tests, 33c225b implementation): the book's chapter, 18 examples, all match; tree-sitter/suite 630 of 639: corpus 452 of 452, highlights 178 of 187 (7 need the locals query, 2 injections); a caret run is checked at its first column (the HTML tests run carets over onclick=). Sizes (stripped / gzipped): sxml.wasm 9,693,235 / 2,006,198, +1,990,621 in code and data since the baseline (the grammars' parse tables 1,770,000 of it, tree-sitter's query code 43,579, the bridge 20,083), budget 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 / 2,800,000; the CLI module 11,289,043 / 2,288,933, budget 9,500,000 / 2,100,000 to 11,500,000 / 2,500,000; the size baseline refreshed.
